correctness.rationale: The example is an ordinary frame example and therefore a scalar-valued g-frame example. Exact enumeration gives positive definite frame operators for every original weaving, with universal bounds (7-sqrt(41))/2 and 4+sqrt(13). Exact inversion of the two individual frame operators gives a canonical-dual weaving whose three vectors are all multiples of e1, so it has no lower frame bound. The common-frame-operator repair follows by evaluating every original weaving at S^{-1}x.

value.rationale: Canonical duals are a central reconstruction object, and Corollary 2.5 claims they can be taken constituent-by-constituent without harming distributed weaving. The counterexample shows qualitative information loss in the smallest natural redundant planar setting: an originally uniformly woven pair acquires a rank-one mixed dual family. The repair identifies the structural issue as incompatibility of the different inverse frame operators and gives a simple condition under which the intended conclusion is valid.
